entities.summary: Theodoric II of Moers (b. 1385) was a prominent entrepreneur and business leader in the Medieval period, shaping the global trade landscape through his ventures and strategic alliances. He played a crucial role in the development of the textile industry, particularly in the production of woolen cloth, and his company, Moers Weavers, became a leading exporter of luxury goods. Theodoric II's innovative approaches to finance and marketing helped establish a new standard for business practices, influencing generations of entrepreneurs to come. His legacy can be seen in the modern textile industry, with many contemporary brands still benefiting from the techniques and strategies he pioneered. Theodoric II's contributions to the global economy have left a lasting impact on the world, making him a notable figure in the annals of business history.
